source_evidence.observation: For a standard normal random variable g and every real t>0, the source gives the two-sided estimate (1/t-1/t^3)(1/sqrt(2π))exp(-t^2/2) ≤ P{g≥t} ≤ (1/t)(1/sqrt(2π))exp(-t^2/2).
The proof writes P{g≥t}=(1/sqrt(2π))∫_t^∞exp(-x^2/2)dx, substitutes x=t+y, bounds exp(-y^2/2) by 1, and evaluates ∫_0^∞exp(-ty)dy=1/t.
The lower bound is obtained from the exact identity ∫_t^∞(1-3x^-4)exp(-x^2/2)dx=(1/t-1/t^3)exp(-t^2/2).

definitions_and_conventions: N(0,1) denotes the standard normal distribution (PDF page 2/printed page 13, Proposition 2.1.2 opening sentence).
P{g≥t} is the one-sided non-strict upper-tail probability (PDF page 2/printed page 13, Proposition 2.1.2 main display).
The standard normal density is (1/sqrt(2π))exp(-x^2/2), as used in the tail-integral formula in the proof (PDF page 2/printed page 13, Proposition 2.1.2 proof).
The factors 1/t-1/t^3 and 1/t multiply the full density value (1/sqrt(2π))exp(-t^2/2) (PDF page 2/printed page 13, Proposition 2.1.2 main display).
implicit_context: The proposition concerns only the upper tail g≥t, not the two-sided tail |g|≥t (PDF page 2/printed page 13, Proposition 2.1.2 main display).
The bounds are exact inequalities valid for every t>0, not asymptotic approximations (PDF page 2/printed page 13, Proposition 2.1.2 main statement).
For 0<t<1 the lower prefactor 1/t-1/t^3 is negative, but the proposition still states the lower bound throughout the full t>0 domain (PDF page 2/printed page 13, Proposition 2.1.2 main statement).

The neighboring 'In particular' display labeled Equation (2.3) is a separate corollary and is excluded from this task's conclusions (PDF page 2/printed page 13, text immediately following the main Proposition 2.1.2 display).

contracts.contract_plain_english: If g is standard normal, then for every t>0 its one-sided upper-tail probability lies between the standard-normal density at t multiplied by 1/t-1/t^3 and the same density multiplied by 1/t. These are exact bounds with the displayed constants (PDF page 2/printed page 13, main display of Proposition 2.1.2).
